roots.origin: 拉丁语 notare（做记号、标注），来自 nota（记号、符号）
roots.core_concept: to mark something so it stands out / 给东西做记号让它突出
roots.core_image: 一只手在一件物品上画下记号，使它从同类中被认出来

roots.origin: 拉丁语 operari（劳作、从事工作），来自 opus（工作、作品）
roots.core_concept: to work, to put effort into function / 让各部分投入运作
roots.core_image: 一双手把部件组合起来并推动，整台系统开始产出结果

roots.origin: 拉丁语 dignus（值得的、配得上的），dignitas（尊严、地位）
roots.core_concept: to be worthy of respect / 一件事或一个人够得上尊重
roots.core_image: 一杆天平，一端是一张面孔或一份成就，另一端放着配得上的荣誉

roots.origin: 拉丁语 ordinare（排列成序、安排），来自 ordo（次序、行列）
roots.core_concept: to lay things out in a sequence / 把事物排成前后有别的次序
roots.core_image: 散乱的物品被一个接一个排成纵列，前后位置分明
roots.english_definition: to arrange in order, set in a row

roots.origin: 拉丁语 solidus（坚实、密实的，无空隙的整体）
roots.core_concept: firm and whole, no hollows / 坚实完整、没有空隙
roots.core_image: 一块厚实的材料，用手按压纹丝不动，内部没有空洞

roots.origin: 拉丁语 terrere（使惊惧、吓住）
roots.core_concept: to fill with a numbing fear / 用巨大的恐惧把人震住
roots.core_image: 黑浪朝人涌来，一瞬间呼吸和动作都被镇住

roots.origin: 拉丁语 rumpere（打断、断裂）及其过去分词 ruptus
roots.core_concept: to break apart suddenly / 使完整的东西猛然断裂
roots.core_image: 一根绷紧的绳索突然从中间断开，两端弹开

roots.origin: 拉丁语 summa（顶端、总数），来自 summus（最高的）
roots.core_concept: the topmost point, then the total that tops up a whole / 最高处，也指汇聚成顶点的总和
roots.core_image: 一枚枚更小的量被叠起来，最高处立着一个代表全部的顶端

concepts.concept: to make a mark so something stands out
concepts.core_image: 物品被画上记号而从同类中被认出

concepts.concept: to work / systems turned to produce a result
concepts.core_image: 部件被组装并推动，系统开始产出结果
天平一端是成就，一端放着配得上的荣誉

concepts.concept: to arrange into an ordered line
concepts.core_image: 散乱物品被排成前后位置分明的纵列
无空洞的厚实材料，按压纹丝不动
巨大威胁逼近，人被镇住难以动弹
绷紧的绳索从中间突然断开

concepts.concept: the total at the top of a stack
concepts.core_image: 众多小量叠起，顶端立着代表全部的总量

words.root_logic: not（做记号）+ -able → 值得被单独做记号记下的
words.origin: 拉丁语 notabilis（值得注意的），来自 notare（做记号）
words.native_definition: worthy of attention or being remembered
words.core_concept: marked out enough to be worth special notice – 被特别标注出来、值得关注的
words.core_image: 人群中一个身影被光标单独圈出，让人记住
examples: The meeting produced a notable breakthrough.
She is a notable figure in the field.
semantic_expansions: 值得注意的/显著的：重要到值得单独做记号
著名的：因突出而被众人记住

words.root_logic: not（记号）+ -ify（使）→ 把一个记号/消息送到某人面前让他知道
words.origin: 晚期拉丁语 notificare（使知道），来自 notare＋facere
words.native_definition: to formally tell someone about something
words.core_concept: bringing a marked message to someone so it becomes known – 把做了记号的信息送到某人眼前
words.core_image: 一封盖着红印章、写着明确消息的信被递到收件人手上
examples: Please notify us of any change of address.
The system notifies users of updates.
semantic_expansions: 通知/告知：把信息正式送到某人面前使其知晓

words.root_logic: not（记号）+ -ion → 心中形成的记号，即一个想法或概念
words.origin: 拉丁语 notio（认识、概念），来自 notus（知道的）
words.native_definition: an idea, belief, or vague understanding
words.core_concept: a mark formed in the mind that stands for an idea – 在脑中成形的、代表某个想法的记号
words.core_image: 一个念头像发光的标签在脑海里亮起
examples: She rejected the notion of fate.
I have no notion of what he means.
semantic_expansions: 概念/观念：心中代表某种理解而成立的记号
想法：脑中浮现的、尚未成形的认识

words.root_logic: not（记号）+ -orious → 被广泛做了记号、名声传开的（多带贬义）
words.origin: 中世纪拉丁语 notorius（尽人皆知的），来自 notus（被知道的）
words.native_definition: famous for something bad
words.core_concept: marked so widely that everyone knows the name – 被处处标注、名声尽人皆知
words.core_image: 一栋建筑的名字反复出现在负面报道的标题上
examples: The city is notorious for traffic jams.
He is a notorious liar.
semantic_expansions: 臭名昭著的：因负面事情名声广为人知

words.root_logic: oper（工作）+ -ate → 让机器或组织进入工作状态
words.origin: 拉丁语 operatus，来自 operari（劳作、工作）
words.native_definition: to control a machine, run a system, or be in working condition
words.core_concept: bringing parts together so a whole begins producing work – 让各部分配合开始产出结果
words.core_image: 驾驶舱里的手推动手柄，整台装置随之启动
examples: She operates the crane safely.
The hospital operates a 24-hour clinic.
semantic_expansions: 操作：控制机器使其按规程工作
运转/经营：系统或组织持续发挥功能

words.root_logic: oper（工作）+ -ation → 使系统工作的过程、活动或手术
words.origin: 拉丁语 operatio（劳作、活动），来自 operari
words.native_definition: the process of working, an organized action, or a medical procedure
words.core_concept: getting parts to cooperate and produce, including the body during surgery – 让部件配合产出结果的一次过程
words.core_image: 一套流程启动，从投入逐步走到产出
examples: The new line is now in operation.
The patient was prepared for operation.
semantic_expansions: 操作/运作：系统投入工作的过程
手术：医生在病人身体上进行的专门操作

words.root_logic: operation（运作）+ -al → 能够执行作业的，或与实际运作有关的
words.origin: 英语 operational，来自 operation
words.native_definition: working and ready to be used, or relating to practical functioning
words.core_concept: able to be put to work now – 此刻就能投入工作的
words.core_image: 指示灯亮起，表示整套系统已就绪可运转
examples: The plant is fully operational again.
We need an operational plan for the launch.
semantic_expansions: 可操作的/运行中的：系统当前能正常执行任务
实际运作的：与执行层面的具体工作有关

words.root_logic: dign（值得）+ -ity（状态）→ 值得尊重并把持住的自身价值
words.origin: 拉丁语 dignitas（尊严、地位），来自 dignus（值得的）
words.native_definition: the state of being worthy of respect, or calm self-respect
words.core_concept: the worth that proves one deserves respect – 经得起检验、配得上尊重的那份价值
words.core_image: 一个人挺直站立，肩头托着的重量与所得尊重相称
examples: She faced the crowd with dignity.
Every person deserves to be treated with dignity.
semantic_expansions: 尊严：证明自己值得被尊重的那份价值
庄重：以稳定姿态撑住这份价值

words.root_logic: in-（不、反对）+ dign（配得上）+ -ant → 因觉得受了不相配的对待而愤怒
words.origin: 拉丁语 indignans（愤愤不平的），来自 indignari（认为不配）
words.native_definition: angry because of unjust or unworthy treatment
words.core_concept: feeling that something is beneath one and thus wrong – 感到被按不配的身价对待而激起愤怒
words.core_image: 一个人自认高出所受待遇，胸口腾起不平之气
examples: She was indignant at the false accusation.
Citizens grew indignant over the unfair tax.
semantic_expansions: 愤慨的/义愤的：因遭遇不相配、不公正的对待而愤怒

words.root_logic: indignant（愤慨）+ -ation → 因不公或轻视而产生的愤怒情绪
words.origin: 拉丁语 indignatio（愤懑），来自 indignari
words.native_definition: anger caused by unworthy or unjust treatment
words.core_concept: the flame kindled when one is treated as beneath one's worth – 被按低劣身价对待时腾起的怒火
words.core_image: 被轻视者胸口涌起的怒火几乎可见
examples: The unfair dismissal caused general indignation.
He reported the news with indignation.
semantic_expansions: 愤慨/义愤：因受到不相配的轻视或不公而生的强烈不满

words.root_logic: ordin（次序）+ -ary（属于…的）→ 依通常次序而来、不越出常规的
words.origin: 拉丁语 ordinarius（按次序的），来自 ordo（次序）
words.native_definition: normal and not special in any way
words.core_concept: following the usual rank and line, nothing extra – 顺着常规次序、没有超出
words.core_image: 一摞日用品按平常位置摆放，没有任何特别标记
examples: In an ordinary year we plant in spring.
The film turned an ordinary story into something moving.
semantic_expansions: 普通的/平常的：顺着通常次序、不特别
平庸的：缺少超出常规的突出点

words.root_logic: co-（共同）+ ordin（次序）+ -ate → 让多方按共同次序配合行动
words.origin: 晚期拉丁语 coordinare（共同排列），来自 ordinare
words.native_definition: to organize different parts so they work together
words.core_concept: putting separate pieces into one shared order so they move as one – 把分散部分排进同一次序协同运作
words.core_image: 几个团队接到同一张时间表，动作因此合到同一节奏
examples: She coordinates the volunteers across three sites.
The rescue teams coordinated their efforts.
semantic_expansions: 协调/配合：把不同部分排进共同次序
使一致：让各方步调对齐

words.root_logic: sub-（在下）+ ordin（次序）→ 排在主序之下、位居从属
words.origin: 拉丁语 subordinatus，来自 subordinare（置于下位）
words.native_definition: lower in rank or position, or a person in such a rank
words.core_concept: placed under the main order – 被排在主序列之下
words.core_image: 一人站在阶梯较下一级，听命于更高位置者的安排
examples: The chief delegate delegated tasks to her subordinates.
Safety is subordinate to the deadline in his logic.
semantic_expansions: 从属的/次要的：排在主序之下
下级：职位处于从属序列的人员

words.root_logic: solid（坚实）→ 质地密实、无空隙，或可靠
words.origin: 拉丁语 solidus（坚实的）
words.native_definition: firm, dense, reliable, and without gaps
words.core_concept: a body with no hollow inside that will not yield to pressure – 内部无空隙、受压力不塌陷
words.core_image: 一块整木被重物压住仍棱角分明，没有变形
examples: The table is made of solid oak.
The proposal rests on solid evidence.
semantic_expansions: 固体的/坚实的：质地密实无空隙
可靠的：像实心结构一样经得起压力

words.root_logic: con-（共同）+ solid（坚实）→ 使分散部分凝成一块坚实整体
words.origin: 拉丁语 consolidare（使牢固）：con- + solidare
words.native_definition: to combine into a stronger whole or make more secure
words.core_concept: pressing separate pieces until they become one solid mass – 让分散部分挤成无空隙的整体
words.core_image: 几处松散的土堆被压成一片结实的路基
examples: The firm consolidated several departments.
Sleep helps consolidate memory.
semantic_expansions: 合并：把分散部分合成一个坚实整体
巩固：让结构或成果变得更牢固

words.root_logic: solid（坚实）+ -arity（状态）→ 众人像一块整体那样彼此支撑
words.origin: 法语 solidarité，来自 solidaire（连带的）
words.native_definition: unity of feeling and support within a group
words.core_concept: a group standing as one dense body where each supports the rest – 大家合成一块整体彼此担当
words.core_image: 许多人并肩站成一面墙，一人受力众人都顶住
examples: Workers showed solidarity during the strike.
We stand in solidarity with the community.
semantic_expansions: 团结/相互支持：众人如一体般彼此坚实支撑

words.root_logic: terr（惊惧）+ -ible（可…的）→ 让人感到惊惧的，或程度极严重
words.origin: 拉丁语 terribilis（可怕的），来自 terrere
words.native_definition: extremely bad, harmful, or causing great fear
words.core_concept: so bad that it overwhelms and frightens – 坏到把人镇住
words.core_image: 一场灾难的场面铺满视野，任何抵抗都显得无力
examples: The storm caused terrible damage.
I had a terrible night's sleep.
semantic_expansions: 可怕的：引发强烈恐惧
严重/糟糕的：坏到接近令人害怕的程度

words.root_logic: terr（惊惧）+ -ify（使）→ 使人充满恐惧
words.origin: 法语 terrifier，来自拉丁语 terrificare
words.native_definition: to make someone feel intense fear
words.core_concept: pouring fear into someone until they freeze – 让恐惧充满一个人直到僵住
words.core_image: 黑影从角落逼近，被看者瞬间屏住呼吸
examples: The loud bang terrified the child.
She was terrified of heights.
semantic_expansions: 使恐惧/使惊吓：用巨大威胁让人充满恐惧

words.root_logic: terr（惊惧）+ -or（名词）→ 极端剧烈的恐惧
words.origin: 拉丁语 terror（惊恐），来自 terrere
words.native_definition: extreme fear, or violence meant to spread such fear
words.core_concept: the frozen state produced by a force too big to face – 面对无法抵挡之物时被镇住的状态
words.core_image: 城市突然笼罩在一种让人无法入睡的惊恐中
examples: The crowd fled in terror.
The group used terror to control the town.
semantic_expansions: 恐怖/惊骇：极端剧烈的恐惧
恐怖行为：以制造恐惧为手段的暴力

words.root_logic: dis-（分开、打散）+ rupt（断裂）→ 打断正常运行
words.origin: 拉丁语 disruptus，来自 disrumpere（裂开、打断）
words.native_definition: to interrupt or throw something out of its normal course
words.core_concept: breaking the continuity of a running system – 把正运行的过程从中间打断
words.core_image: 正在亮起的长串灯忽然断掉几盏，节奏被打乱
examples: Flights were disrupted by the storm.
The protest disrupted traffic.
semantic_expansions: 扰乱/打断：使正常运行从中间断开
中断：使连续性暂时或永久停止

words.root_logic: ab-（离开）+ rupt（断裂）→ 像被硬生生掐断、缺乏过渡
words.origin: 拉丁语 abruptus（断裂的），来自 abrumpere（切断）
words.native_definition: sudden, unexpected, and lacking smooth transition
words.core_concept: cut off sharply without the usual lead-in – 没有过渡就硬生生断掉
words.core_image: 一条平整的山路走到底突然断成悬崖边缘
examples: The meeting came to an abrupt end.
His tone was abrupt and cold.
semantic_expansions: 突然的/生硬的：像被硬生生断开、缺少过渡
陡峭的：地形如断裂般骤然下降

words.root_logic: cor-（完全）+ rupt（断裂）→ 使原本正直的东西整体腐坏变形
words.origin: 拉丁语 corruptus，来自 corrumpere（败坏）
words.native_definition: dishonest or morally decayed, or data that has been damaged
words.core_concept: breaking down a sound whole, morally or materially – 把一个完好整体从内部败坏
words.core_image: 原本明亮的证书被墨渍和篡改弄得形状歪曲
examples: Corrupt officials were removed from office.
The file was corrupt and could not be opened.
semantic_expansions: 腐败的/腐化的：整体从内部败坏
损坏的：数据或物品被破坏到无法正常用

words.root_logic: sum（总数）→ 若干部分加在一起得到的总量
words.origin: 拉丁语 summa（总数、顶端）
words.native_definition: the total amount from adding parts, or an amount of money
words.core_concept: the top result reached when all parts are piled together – 各部分相加后处于顶端的那个总值
words.core_image: 一叠小账单被整齐相加，顶端得出一个数字
examples: The sum of the parts equals the whole.
He paid a large sum for the house.
semantic_expansions: 总和：各部分组成的总量
金额：一笔具体数额的钱

words.root_logic: summary（概要）+ -ize（使）→ 把大量内容收拢成一段简短总说
words.origin: 英语 summarize，来自 summary
words.native_definition: to state the main points briefly
words.core_concept: gathering a long account into a single top-line statement – 把长内容收拢成顶端的简要概括
words.core_image: 成堆文字被压成一行要点，整齐排在顶部
examples: Summarize the key findings in two sentences.
The report summarizes five years of data.
semantic_expansions: 总结/概括：把大量内容收拢成简短的要点

words.root_logic: sum（总数）+ -mary → 把内容汇总成简短整体
words.origin: 中世纪拉丁语 summarius（概要的），来自 summa（总数）
words.native_definition: a brief statement of the main points
words.core_concept: the compact total of a longer account – 长内容汇总出的简短总体
words.core_image: 一本书的末页浓缩了全部章节的要点
examples: Each chapter ends with a summary.
She gave a brief summary of the case.
semantic_expansions: 摘要/概要：把完整内容浓缩成的简要总体

words.root_logic: fin（终结、结清）+ -ance → 与清偿/资金结算有关的事务
words.origin: 中古法语 finance（结算），来自 finer（终结、清账）
words.native_definition: the management of money, or money provided for a purpose
words.core_concept: the money side of seeing a matter through to its end – 把事项推进到收尾时的资金支撑
words.core_image: 一张建造计划下方垫着一层钱物，支撑它进行到完工
examples: She studied finance at university.
The project needs public finance.
semantic_expansions: 金融/财政：围绕资金收付与管理的事务
资金：支撑事项完成所需的款项

words.root_logic: com-（共同）+ part（部分）+ -ment → 大空间被划分出的一个部分
words.origin: 法语 compartiment，来自 compartir（分割）
words.native_definition: a separate section, often given a specific use
words.core_concept: one divided-out pocket inside a larger whole – 大整体中切分出的一块空位
words.core_image: 列车长椅上方被隔板分成一个个独立空间
examples: The fridge has a separate compartment for vegetables.
Her bag has a hidden compartment.
semantic_expansions: 隔间/车厢：大空间中被划分出的独立部分

words.root_logic: counter-（对应、对照）+ part（部分）→ 与某部分相对称的对应部分
words.origin: 英语 counterpart，来自 counter ＋ part
words.native_definition: a person or thing that corresponds to another in position or function
words.core_concept: the matching part standing opposite across a shared scheme – 在共同结构中与一方成对的另一半
words.core_image: 谈判桌两边各坐一人，职位一一对应
examples: The US secretary met his British counterpart.
This gear is the counterpart of that one.
semantic_expansions: 对应的人/物：在共同结构中与另一方地位、功能相对的部分

words.root_logic: per-（贯穿）+ pet（追求）+ -ual → 一直向前追着不停，没有终止
words.origin: 拉丁语 perpetuus（连续的），可能与 per＋petere 相关
words.native_definition: continuing forever, or seeming to never end
words.core_concept: stretching forward without a breaking point – 一路向前不断开
words.core_image: 一条线向前延展到望不见尽头的位置
examples: The clock is driven by a near-perpetual motion.
He complained about the perpetual noise.
semantic_expansions: 永恒的/永久的：向前不断开、没有终止
不断的：持续发生而看上去无尽头

words.root_logic: ad-（靠向）+ ject（投掷）→ 原意“加靠到名词旁的词”
words.origin: 拉丁语 adjectivum（附加的词），来自 adjicere（添加）
words.native_definition: a word that modifies a noun by adding a quality
words.core_concept: a word thrown alongside a noun to add description – 投过去依附在名词旁起修饰作用的词
words.core_image: “blue”被放到“sky”旁边，天空的颜色就此明确
examples: In English, adjectives usually precede the noun.
The adjective modifies the noun.
semantic_expansions: 形容词：投放到名词旁、为其添加描述的词

words.root_logic: direct（指引）+ -ory（场所）→ 用来指引人找到对象的名册或路径组织
words.origin: 中世纪拉丁语 directorium（指引的书册），来自 dirigere（指引）
words.native_definition: a listing of names or files used to find things
words.core_concept: an organized place that points one toward the sought item – 帮你指向目标所在的编排
words.core_image: 大厅里的名册按姓氏排列，一翻就能指向对应房间
examples: Please check the directory for the extension.
Save the file into a new directory.
semantic_expansions: 名录/目录：按规则编排、指引人找到对象的集合
文件夹：计算机中指向并组织文件的位置
